title: Logos
text: Logos is a Python library for writing mathematical arguments that an independent checker can verify. This book starts with a small proof and builds toward number theory and program contracts. It is also available as a single PDF.

title: Introduction
text: Suppose your assumptions are and , and your goal is . On paper you apply the implication to . In Logos you propose that same step, pointing to where you got each premise. The checker confirms that both premises are available and computes the conclusion . If you claim that this application yields , the checker rejects the step because the implication concludes .

title: Two programs, two jobs
text: Python produces the derivation. You can write the steps yourself, call a tactic, or ask a search procedure or language model to propose them. If search stops without a derivation, you still have an open question. Unsuccessful search leaves both the claim and its negation unproved by that search. The independent Rust checker reads the proposed derivation. It recomputes what each rule concludes from its inputs and checks that the final conclusion matches the stated theorem. Your Python runs when producing evidence. The checker runs separately on the resulting artifact.

title: What the trusted checker owns
text: The trusted checker implements a fixed set of rules for logic and arithmetic. Applying an implication is one of those rules. The artifact records the theorem, its declarations, and the steps proposed as evidence. The Rust checker reads that portable record and checks the derivation. Names, comments and tactics in Python help you produce or explain it.

title: What a receipt is
text: After acceptance, Logos stores a receipt with the exact artifact bytes and their SHA-256 digest. You can inspect the receipt to ask the checker to recheck those saved bytes and explain the accepted derivation. Here is how to read three parts of a result for the argument above, summarized in words. Statement. For any propositions and , if holds and holds, then follows. Evidence. Introduce each premise as a local hypothesis, apply the implication, and account for those hypotheses in the conditional conclusion. Axiom status. Zero custom axioms. The two local hypotheses appear as premises of the s

title: Scope
text: The checker covers propositional logic, equality, integer arithmetic and order, transparent definitions, primitive recursion on the natural numbers, integer quantifiers, and contracts for supported Python functions and loops. Sets, real analysis, quotient types and general recursion are outside this scope. The chapter on cases shows how a checked counterexample can settle a question that unsuccessful proof search leaves open.

title: Conventions
text: In Python, a Logos proposition is a symbolic expression. For example, P >> Q builds an implication from symbolic propositions. Python does not evaluate it to a Boolean truth value. Build and check a theorem in the Quick Start. For lookup, use the Public API Reference or the checker’s --help.

text: The proposed application is invalid. The implication yields . The search found no proof before it stopped. The status of is still open on that evidence. The checker verified the derivation using the declared custom axiom as an assumption.

text: A disjunction says that one of two things is true, but it does not say which. A proof that uses a disjunction must work in both cases. title: Witnesses and Their Scope
text: An existential statement promises a value. It does not say which one, and it does not let you keep the value after the promise is discharged. This chapter introduces the two directions of that promise: opening an existential that you already have, and closing an existential that you need to prove. It also introduces the universal quantifier inside a proof and the scope rules that keep witnesses from leaking.

title: Definitions That Unfold, Lemmas You Can Name
text: A definition is not an assumption. It is a name for a body, and the checker may replace the name with the body whenever it needs to compare two statements. A lemma is not a shortcut either: it is a separately checked theorem whose conclusion another proof may cite. This chapter uses both to build a small theory of divisibility.

text: Is even? You can compute it. A proof has to answer the same question for a letter , without knowing which integer it names. Number theory begins when we stop computing examples and start describing the shape of a number: one quotient, one remainder, one product. This chapter uses the divisibility lemmas from Chapter 6 to reason about even and odd integers.

page: Extend the Checked Language with a Domain
title: Limits
text: The domain models closed integer intervals. It does not model real time, time zones, durations, exclusive endpoints, recurring bookings or the database that stores them. A checked overlap claim is a statement about the model, not a guarantee that the booking service is deployed correctly. The tactic is a certificate builder, not a decision procedure. It closes overlap goals whose sides follow from order facts by exact linear arithmetic. It does not search for a witness, split on cases, or prove a negated overlap. A failed call leaves the theorem uncertified; it does not prove the negation.

title: logos.authoring.ProofContext
text: Import with from logos.authoring import ProofContext. ProofContext(statement: Expr, binders: tuple[Var, ...], theorem: str, fn=None) The p argument supplied to a proof function by @theorem_name.proof. Its goal and available facts change as you introduce assumptions and enter scopes.

title: ProofContext.note
text: note(text: str) -> None on ProofContext. Attach authored commentary after the most recently derived fact.

title: ProofContext.assume
text: assume(proposition: Expr) -> Fact on ProofContext. Introduce the antecedent of the current implication as a local fact and leave the consequent as the goal. The supplied proposition must match the antecedent.

title: ProofContext.obtain
text: obtain(existential: Fact) -> tuple[Var, Fact] on ProofContext. Open a fact of shape ∃x. P(x), returning a fresh local variable and a fact for its instantiated predicate. The symbol is scoped to the elimination: it cannot appear free in the conclusion.

title: ProofContext.apply
text: apply(lemma, *arguments) -> Fact on ProofContext. Instantiate a checked theorem (or local implication fact) step by step.

title: ProofContext.and_intro
text: and_intro(left: Fact, right: Fact) -> Fact on ProofContext. Combine two facts for A and B into a fact for A & B.

title: ProofContext.exists
text: exists(goal: Expr, value: Expr, evidence: Fact) -> Fact on ProofContext. Given ∃x. P(x), a value, and a Fact proving P(value), return a Fact for the existential without closing the current goal. A Python literal is lifted. A non-existential target reports exists_goal, and an out-of-scope value reports witness_escape. Mismatched evidence reports evidence_mismatch. See the complete examples.

title: ProofContext.subst
text: subst(fact: Fact, equality: Fact) -> Fact on ProofContext. Replace one side of an equality throughout a fact.

title: ProofContext.refl
text: refl(expression: Expr) -> Fact on ProofContext. Return a fact proving the expression equal to itself.

title: ProofContext.symm
text: symm(fact: Fact) -> Fact on ProofContext. Reverse an equality fact. Other fact shapes fail.

title: ProofContext.trans
text: trans(left: Fact, right: Fact) -> Fact on ProofContext. Compose two equality facts at their matching middle expression. Non-equalities and mismatched middle expressions fail.

title: ProofContext.not_elim
text: not_elim(negation: Fact, premise: Fact) -> Fact on ProofContext. From facts for ¬P and P, return a fact for falsehood. The operands must match.

title: ProofContext.ex_falso
text: ex_falso(falsehood: Fact) -> Fact on ProofContext. Use a fact for falsehood to obtain a fact for the current goal. Requires an open goal.

title: ProofContext.not_lt_of_lt
text: not_lt_of_lt(low: Expr, high: Expr, fact: Fact) -> Fact on ProofContext. From low < high derive ~(high < low) without a new axiom.

title: ProofContext.order
text: order(law: str, *args, using=()) -> Fact on ProofContext. Cite a core order law with explicit integer arguments and premises.

title: ProofContext.linear
text: linear(goal: Expr, *, using=()) -> Fact on ProofContext. Prove a linear inequality from named facts with a checked certificate.

title: ProofContext.recursor_base
text: recursor_base(function) -> Fact on ProofContext. Return the defining equality of the indicated recursor at zero.

title: ProofContext.recursor_step
text: recursor_step(function, argument: Expr, nonnegative: Fact) -> Fact on ProofContext. Return the defining equality at the successor of the supplied argument. Supply a fact establishing that the argument is nonnegative.

title: ProofContext.rewrite
text: rewrite(fact: Fact, equality: Fact) -> Fact on ProofContext. Rewrite the second argument of a transparent divides fact.

title: ProofContext.least
text: least(lower: Expr, nonempty: Fact) -> Fact on ProofContext. Apply the least-element rule to a nonempty bounded predicate.

title: ProofContext.fix
text: fix(name: str='x') -> '_Fixed' on ProofContext. Enter a universal goal with with p.fix(name) as scope. Use the fresh symbol scope.variable and call scope.finish(evidence) inside the block. Read scope.result afterward. Other goal shapes fail.

title: ProofContext.negate
text: negate(statement: Expr | None=None) -> '_Negation' on ProofContext. Enter a negation goal with its operand as a local assumption. Derive a contradiction inside the block.

title: ProofContext.cases
text: cases(disjunction: Fact) -> '_Cases' on ProofContext. Split a disjunction fact into two branches. Prove the same conclusion with the left alternative in one branch and the right in the other.

title: ProofContext.contradict
text: contradict(proposition: Expr) -> '_Contradiction' on ProofContext. Enter a branch with the given proposition assumed and derive falsehood to discharge that assumption.

title: ProofContext.induction
text: induction(variable: Var, lower=0, *, nonnegative: Fact | None=None) -> '_Induction' on ProofContext. Use integer induction from lower on the goal's variable. Prove the goal at the lower bound in ind.base(), and prove it at the successor from the induction hypothesis in ind.step(). Supply an appropriate lower-bound fact when it is not already available. See the factorial proof.

title: ProofContext.ring
text: ring(equation: Expr, *, using=()) -> Fact on ProofContext. Return a fact for an integer polynomial equality, optionally using equality facts. If normalization cannot establish the identity, the proof step fails.

title: ProofContext.witness
text: witness(value: Expr, evidence: Fact | ProofTerm) -> ProofTerm on ProofContext. For the current goal ∃x. P(x), supply a value and evidence for P(value), then return the resulting proof term. A Python literal is lifted. Diagnostics include witness_goal for the wrong goal shape, witness_escape for an out-of-scope value, and witness_mismatch for a fact that proves the wrong predicate. See the complete examples.

title: Tactics
text: A tactic receives a Goal and returns evidence or subgoals with a function to compose their evidence. Supply tactics in order to the runner. A failed step raises TacticFailed and a sequence with unclosed goals fails certification. See the complete examples.

title: logos.tactics.all_goals
text: Import with from logos.tactics import all_goals. all_goals(tactic_fn) Apply tactic_fn to each open subgoal (for use after a splitting tactic).

title: logos.tactics.andL
text: Import with from logos.tactics import andL. andL(hyp_name: str, result_name: str) Extract left conjunct: from h: A & B, add result_name: A.

title: logos.tactics.andR
text: Import with from logos.tactics import andR. andR(hyp_name: str, result_name: str) Extract right conjunct: from h: A & B, add result_name: B.

title: logos.tactics.apply
text: Import with from logos.tactics import apply. apply(ref) Apply a theorem/axiom/hypothesis to close or transform the goal.

title: logos.tactics.assumption
text: Import with from logos.tactics import assumption. assumption() Return a tactic that closes a goal with a matching local hypothesis, or fails if none matches.

title: logos.tactics.auto
text: Import with from logos.tactics import auto. auto(*hints, depth: int=5, timeout: float | None=None) Automatic tactic. Tries a cascade of strategies up to depth search levels.

title: logos.tactics.cases
text: Import with from logos.tactics import cases. cases(hyp_name: str, case_name: str='h') Build a piecewise symbolic expression from condition/value pairs and a default value.

title: logos.tactics.conj
text: Import with from logos.tactics import conj. conj(h1: str, h2: str, result_name: str) Conjunction intro: from h1: A and h2: B, add result_name: A & B.

title: logos.tactics.contradiction
text: Import with from logos.tactics import contradiction. contradiction() Return a tactic that closes a goal using a contradiction derivable from its local hypotheses. Fails if it cannot find one.

title: logos.tactics.decide
text: Import with from logos.tactics import decide. decide() Test a closed Boolean proposition as a tactic. False or unsupported propositions fail. A successful test returns legacy evidence that does not certify the proposition under Rust replay. For portable integer inequalities use ProofContext.linear.

title: logos.tactics.eval_
text: Import with from logos.tactics import eval_. eval_() Evaluate ground (variable-free) arithmetic sub-expressions, then close with Refl.

title: logos.tactics.exact
text: Import with from logos.tactics import exact. exact(term: ProofTerm) Return a tactic that supplies the given proof term for checker validation against the current goal.

title: logos.tactics.first
text: Import with from logos.tactics import first. first(*tactics) Try each tactic in order; succeed with the first that doesn't raise TacticFailed.

title: logos.tactics.have
text: Import with from logos.tactics import have. have(new_name: str, impl_hyp: str, ant_hyp: str) Forward modus ponens: from impl_hyp: A→B and ant_hyp: A, add new_name: B.

title: logos.tactics.intro
text: Import with from logos.tactics import intro. intro(*names: str) Return a tactic that opens one universal binder, implication, or negation per supplied name. Continue with the body or consequent, or with falsehood for a negation. Unsupported goal shapes fail.

title: logos.tactics.left
text: Import with from logos.tactics import left. left(right_type: Expr) Return a tactic that chooses the left side of a disjunction and leaves that side as a goal. Pass the right proposition as right_type.

title: logos.tactics.linarith
text: Import with from logos.tactics import linarith. linarith() Search for a linear arithmetic consequence of local hypotheses. Unsupported goals or failed searches raise TacticFailed. The legacy evidence returned on success does not certify the inequality under Rust replay. Use ProofContext.linear for portable certificates.

title: logos.tactics.norm_num
text: Import with from logos.tactics import norm_num. norm_num() Normalize numeric literals and close if equal.

title: logos.tactics.order
text: Import with from logos.tactics import order. order(law: str) Close a strict-order goal with one core order law.

title: logos.tactics.refl
text: Import with from logos.tactics import refl. refl() Return a tactic that closes an equality with structurally identical sides. Other goal shapes fail.

title: logos.tactics.repeat
text: Import with from logos.tactics import repeat. repeat(tactic_fn) Apply tactic_fn until it fails; apply all successful steps.

title: logos.tactics.rewrite
text: Import with from logos.tactics import rewrite. rewrite(ref) Rewrite left-to-right using a named equation or Axiom/Theorem object.

title: logos.tactics.rewrite_rev
text: Import with from logos.tactics import rewrite_rev. rewrite_rev(ref) Rewrite right-to-left using a named equation or Axiom/Theorem object.

title: logos.tactics.right
text: Import with from logos.tactics import right. right(left_type: Expr) Return a tactic that chooses the right side of a disjunction and leaves that side as a goal. Pass the left proposition as left_type.

title: logos.tactics.ring
text: Import with from logos.tactics import ring. ring() Return a tactic that closes integer polynomial equalities such as a*m + b*m == (a+b)*m. A non-equality or distinct polynomial normal forms fail. See the complete divisibility proof for the corresponding proof-context operation.

title: logos.tactics.split
text: Import with from logos.tactics import split. split() Return a tactic for A & B that opens A and B as subgoals in that order. Other goal shapes fail.

title: logos.tactics.then
text: Import with from logos.tactics import then. then(*tactics) Apply tactics in sequence to the current goal (as a single compound tactic).

title: logos.tactics.try_
text: Import with from logos.tactics import try_. try_(tactic_fn) Apply tactic_fn; if it fails, return a no-op (transforms goal to itself).

title: logos.tactics.unfold
text: Import with from logos.tactics import unfold. unfold(*refs) Replace App(name, args) nodes with the function's definition body.

title: logos.tactics.witness
text: Import with from logos.tactics import witness. witness(val: Expr) Return a tactic for an existential goal ∃x. P(x). Pass a symbolic value such as lit(5). The tactic opens one subgoal P(value) with the same hypotheses; the next tactic supplies its evidence. Other goal shapes raise TacticFailed with witness: expected Exists. The checker validates the witness sort and evidence. See the complete examples.
